questions.q: What actually controls who can see a given report?
options: A sharing checkbox on the report itself
The folder the report is saved in
The report type it was built from
The user's profile alone, regardless of folders
questions.explain: Reports don't carry their own sharing setting. Visibility is controlled by the folder a report is saved into and how that folder is shared.

questions.q: Which access level lets someone run a report but not edit or move it?
options: Manager
Editor
Viewer
Owner
questions.explain: Viewer is read-only: it lets someone run reports in the folder without being able to change or relocate them. Editor and Manager both allow changes, with Manager adding re-sharing rights.

questions.q: A folder is shared with the Eastern Sales Team at Viewer access. A new subfolder is created inside it with no changes made. What happens to sharing on the subfolder?
options: It starts completely private until shared manually
It automatically inherits the parent folder's sharing
It defaults to Manager access for everyone
It can't be created until sharing is set explicitly
questions.explain: Subfolders inherit their parent folder's sharing settings by default, so the Eastern Sales Team gets the same Viewer access without any extra configuration.

questions.q: What's the main risk of saving a report straight into a broadly shared folder before it's finished?
options: The report will be automatically deleted after a week
Nothing — reports are private until explicitly published
It becomes visible to everyone that folder is already shared with, immediately
It can only be viewed by the report's creator
questions.explain: A report's audience is whatever the folder's audience already is. There's no separate publish step — the moment it's saved there, it's visible to that folder's full audience.

questions.q: Which access level would you give a folder of finished dashboards meant for executives to browse but never modify?
options: Manager
Editor
Viewer
No access level is needed for read-only use
questions.explain: Viewer grants exactly what's needed here: the ability to open and run what's in the folder without being able to change its contents.
